sanskrit: bhāryā me bhava suśroṇi tyajainān sukham āpnuhi akhilān sindhusauvīrān avāpnuhi mayā saha
english: "Become my wife, O fair-hipped one; abandon these men and enjoy happiness. Come with me and obtain all the lands of the Sindhu and the Sauvīras."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktā sindhurājena vākyaṃ hṛdayakampanam kṛṣṇā tasmād apākrāmad deśāt sabhrukuṭīmukhī
english: Vaiśampāyana said: Thus addressed by the king of Sindhu with words that made the heart tremble, Kṛṣṇā moved away from that spot with furrowed brows.

sanskrit: avamatyāsya tad vākyam ākṣipya ca sumadhyamā maivam ity abravīt kṛṣṇā lajjasveti ca saindhavam
english: Scorning his words and rebuking him, the slender-waisted Kṛṣṇā said to the king of Sindhu, "Do not do this — be ashamed!"

sanskrit: sā kāṅkṣamāṇā bhartṝṇām upayānam aninditā vilobhayām āsa paraṃ vākyair vākyāni yuñjatī
english: She, the blameless one, longing for the arrival of her husbands, tried to dissuade him further by joining her words of rebuke with words of persuasion.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca saroṣarāgopahatena valgunā; sarāganetreṇa natonnatabhruvā mukhena visphūrya suvīrarāṣṭrapaṃ; tato 'bravīt taṃ drupadātmajā punaḥ
english: Vaiśampāyana said: With a lovely face flushed with anger and passion, with eyes reddened and brows knit high and low, turning her face fully toward the lord of the Sauvīra realm, the daughter of Drupada then spoke again.

sanskrit: yaśasvinas tīkṣṇaviṣān mahārathān; adhikṣipan mūḍha na lajjase katham mahendrakalpān niratān svakarmasu; sthitān samūheṣv api yakṣarakṣasām
english: "Reviling those illustrious great warriors, sharp as venom, equal to Mahendra, devoted to their own duties, who stand firm even among hosts of yakṣas and rākṣasas — how, O fool, are you not ashamed?"

sanskrit: na kiṃ cid īḍyaṃ pravadanti pāpaṃ; vanecaraṃ vā gṛhamedhinaṃ vā tapasvinaṃ saṃparipūrṇavidyaṃ; bhaṣanti haivaṃ śvanarāḥ suvīra
english: "Dogs speak so even of praiseworthy men — whether a forest-dweller, a householder, or an ascetic fully accomplished in learning. They bark without praising anything good, O king of the Sauvīras."

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu manye tava nāsti kaś cid; etādṛśe kṣatriyasaṃniveśe yas tvādya pātālamukhe patantaṃ; pāṇau gṛhītvā pratisaṃhareta
english: "I think there is no one among such an assembly of kṣatriyas who could today seize your falling hand as you tumble toward the mouth of hell and pull you back."

sanskrit: nāgaṃ prabhinnaṃ girikūṭakalpam; upatyakāṃ haimavatīṃ carantam daṇḍīva yūthād apasedhase tvaṃ; yo jetum āśaṃsasi dharmarājam
english: "You, who aspire to conquer Dharmarāja, are like one who tries to drive away with a stick a maddened elephant, mountain-like, roaming the Himalayan slopes from its herd."

sanskrit: bālyāt prasuptasya mahābalasya; siṃhasya pakṣmāṇi mukhāl lunāsi padā samāhatya palāyamānaḥ; kruddhaṃ yadā drakṣyasi bhīmasenam
english: "You pluck the eyelashes from the mouth of a mighty sleeping lion — and then you flee on foot. When you see Bhīmasena in his wrath, what will become of you?"

sanskrit: mahābalaṃ ghorataraṃ pravṛddhaṃ; jātaṃ hariṃ parvatakandareṣu prasuptam ugraṃ prapadena haṃsi; yaḥ kruddham āsetsyasi jiṣṇum ugram
english: "You strike with your toe-tip a terrible, fully-grown, mighty lion born in mountain caves while it sleeps — you who would dare to approach the fierce and enraged Jiṣṇu."

sanskrit: kṛṣṇoragau tīkṣṇaviṣān dvijihvau; mattaḥ padākrāmasi pucchadeśe yaḥ pāṇḍavābhyāṃ puruṣottamābhyāṃ; jaghanyajābhyāṃ prayuyutsase tvam
english: "You recklessly tread upon the tails of two sharp-fanged, dark cobras with keen venom — you who would fight with the two younger-born among the Pāṇḍavas, those best of men."

sanskrit: yathā ca veṇuḥ kadalī nalo vā; phalanty abhāvāya na bhūtaye ''tmanaḥ tathaiva māṃ taiḥ parirakṣyamāṇām; ādāsyase karkaṭakīva garbham
english: "Just as the bamboo, the plantain, and the reed bear fruit only for their own destruction and not for their flourishing, so you will seize me who am protected by them — and it will bring about your end, like the womb of a she-crab."

sanskrit: jayadratha uvāca jānāmi kṛṣṇe viditaṃ mamaitad; yathāvidhās te naradevaputrāḥ na tv evam etena vibhīṣaṇena; śakyā vayaṃ trāsayituṃ tvayādya
english: Jayadratha said: "I know it, Kṛṣṇā, I know well what manner of men are these sons of the god-king. Yet we cannot be frightened today by you with this boasting and threatening."

sanskrit: vayaṃ punaḥ saptadaśeṣu kṛṣṇe; kuleṣu sarve 'navameṣu jātāḥ ṣaḍbhyo guṇebhyo 'bhyadhikā vihīnān; manyāmahe draupadi pāṇḍuputrān
english: "We, O Kṛṣṇā, are all born in seventeen illustrious clans. We consider the sons of Pāṇḍu, O Draupadī, inferior to us in six virtues and more."

sanskrit: sā kṣipram ātiṣṭha gajaṃ rathaṃ vā; na vākyamātreṇa vayaṃ hi śakyāḥ āśaṃsa vā tvaṃ kṛpaṇaṃ vadantī; sauvīrarājasya punaḥ prasādam
english: "So quickly mount an elephant or a chariot — we cannot be stopped by words alone. Or beg piteously and seek once more the grace of the king of the Sauvīras."

sanskrit: draupady uvāca mahābalā kiṃ tv iha durbaleva; sauvīrarājasya matāham asmi yāhaṃ pramāthād iha saṃpratītā; sauvīrarājaṃ kṛpaṇaṃ vadeyam
english: Draupadī said: "Though mighty, shall I appear weak here? Shall I, who am known for my valor, beg piteously of the king of the Sauvīras? Am I so regarded by the king of the Sauvīras?"

sanskrit: yasyā hi kṛṣṇau padavīṃ caretāṃ; samāsthitāv ekarathe sahāyau indro 'pi tāṃ nāpaharet kathaṃ cin; manuṣyamātraḥ kṛpaṇaḥ kuto 'nyaḥ
english: "She in whose steps Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna — allies seated together on one chariot — would follow: even Indra could not carry her away; how then any mere mortal, let alone this wretch?"

sanskrit: yadā kirīṭī paravīraghātī; nighnan rathastho dviṣatāṃ manāṃsi madantare tvaddhvajinīṃ praveṣṭā; kakṣaṃ dahann agnir ivoṣṇageṣu
english: "When Kirīṭī, the slayer of enemy heroes, standing in his chariot and crushing the hearts of foes, enters your army to find me — like fire burning through dry grass in summer heat —"

sanskrit: janārdanasyānugā vṛṣṇivīrā; maheṣvāsāḥ kekayāś cāpi sarve ete hi sarve mama rājaputrāḥ; prahṛṣṭarūpāḥ padavīṃ careyuḥ
english: "— all the Vṛṣṇi heroes who follow Janārdana, the great bowmen and the Kekaya warriors too — all these princes of mine would joyfully follow his track."

sanskrit: maurvīvisṛṣṭāḥ stanayitnughoṣā; gāṇḍīvamuktās tv ativegavantaḥ hastaṃ samāhatya dhanaṃjayasya; bhīmāḥ śabdaṃ ghorataraṃ nadanti
english: "The terrible arrows released from the Gāṇḍīva bow, loosed from the bowstring with the roar of thunder, of exceeding swiftness, strike Dhanañjaya's hand and roar with a sound most dreadful."

sanskrit: gāṇḍīvamuktāṃś ca mahāśaraughān; pataṃgasaṃghān iva śīghravegān saśaṅkhaghoṣaḥ satalatraghoṣo; gāṇḍīvadhanvā muhur udvamaṃś ca yadā śarān arpayitā tavorasi; tadā manas te kim ivābhaviṣyat
english: "The mighty torrents of arrows released from the Gāṇḍīva, swift as swarms of locusts — when the Gāṇḍīva-bearer, blowing his conch and sounding his palm-guard, repeatedly pours those arrows upon your chest, what then will become of your spirit?"

sanskrit: gadāhastaṃ bhīmam abhidravantaṃ; mādrīputrau saṃpatantau diśaś ca amarṣajaṃ krodhaviṣaṃ vamantau; dṛṣṭvā ciraṃ tāpam upaiṣyase 'dhama
english: "Seeing Bhīma rushing at you with mace in hand, the two sons of Mādrī flying at you from all directions, spewing the venom of their indignant rage — you will suffer long torment, O wretch."

sanskrit: yathā cāhaṃ nāticare kathaṃ cit; patīn mahārhān manasāpi jātu tenādya satyena vaśīkṛtaṃ tvāṃ; draṣṭāsmi pārthaiḥ parikṛṣyamāṇam
english: "And just as I would never transgress in any way my most worthy husbands — not even in my mind — by that truth I shall today see you subdued and dragged away by the Pārthas."

sanskrit: na saṃbhramaṃ gantum ahaṃ hi śakṣye; tvayā nṛśaṃsena vikṛṣyamāṇā samāgatāhaṃ hi kurupravīraiḥ; punar vanaṃ kāmyakam āgatā ca
english: "I shall not flee in confusion though dragged away by you, O cruel one. For I have come together with the foremost heroes of the Kuru line and have returned to the Kāmyaka forest."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sā tān anuprekṣya viśālanetrā; jighṛkṣamāṇān avabhartsayantī provāca mā mā spṛśateti bhītā; dhaumyaṃ pracukrośa purohitaṃ sā
english: Vaiśampāyana said: The wide-eyed one glanced at them as they reached out to seize her, rebuking them; frightened, she cried out "Touch me not! Touch me not!" and called loudly to Dhaumya, the family priest.

sanskrit: jagrāha tām uttaravastradeśe; jayadrathas taṃ samavākṣipat sā tayā samākṣiptatanuḥ sa pāpaḥ; papāta śākhīva nikṛttamūlaḥ
english: Jayadratha seized her by the hem of her upper garment; she wrenched herself away — and that sinful one, his body jerked by her, fell like a tree with its roots cut through.

sanskrit: pragṛhyamāṇā tu mahājavena; muhur viniḥśvasya ca rājaputrī sā kṛṣyamāṇā ratham āruroha; dhaumyasya pādāv abhivādya kṛṣṇā
english: Yet seized with great force, the royal daughter Kṛṣṇā heaved repeated sighs; dragged along, she was made to mount the chariot — though not before she bowed at the feet of Dhaumya.

sanskrit: dhaumya uvāca neyaṃ śakyā tvayā netum avijitya mahārathān dharmaṃ kṣatrasya paurāṇam avekṣasva jayadratha
english: Dhaumya said: "She cannot be taken by you without first conquering those great warriors. Reflect on the ancient duty of the kṣatriya order, Jayadratha."

sanskrit: kṣudraṃ kṛtvā phalaṃ pāpaṃ prāpsyasi tvam asaṃśayam āsādya pāṇḍavān vīrān dharmarājapurogamān
english: "Having committed this base act, you will without doubt reap a sinful fruit when you encounter those heroic Pāṇḍavas led by Dharmarāja."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktvā hriyamāṇāṃ tāṃ rājaputrīṃ yaśasvinīm anvagacchat tadā dhaumyaḥ padātigaṇamadhyagaḥ
english: Vaiśampāyana said: Having spoken thus, Dhaumya then followed that illustrious royal princess as she was being carried away, walking in the midst of the foot-soldiers.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato diśaḥ saṃpravihṛtya pārthā; mṛgān varāhān mahiṣāṃś ca hatvā dhanurdharāḥ śreṣṭhatamāḥ pṛthivyāṃ; pṛthak carantaḥ sahitā babhūvuḥ
english: Vaiśampāyana said: Then the Pārthas, having ranged in all directions — those foremost bowmen on earth — slaying deer, boars, and buffaloes while roaming separately, came together again.

sanskrit: tato mṛgavyālagaṇānukīrṇaṃ; mahāvanaṃ tad vihagopaghuṣṭam bhrātṝṃś ca tān abhyavadad yudhiṣṭhiraḥ; śrutvā giro vyāharatāṃ mṛgāṇām
english: Then, in that great forest thronging with deer and snakes and echoing with the cries of birds, Yudhiṣṭhira addressed those brothers, having heard the voices of the deer calling out.

sanskrit: ādityadīptāṃ diśam abhyupetya; mṛgadvijāḥ krūram ime vadanti āyāsam ugraṃ prativedayanto; mahāhavaṃ śatrubhir vāvamānam
english: "Turning toward the direction lit by the sun, the deer and birds speak harshly, foretelling a terrible ordeal — a great battle with enemies, or an insult suffered."

sanskrit: kṣipraṃ nivartadhvam alaṃ mṛgair no; mano hi me dūyati dahyate ca buddhiṃ samācchādya ca me samanyur; uddhūyate prāṇapatiḥ śarīre
english: "Turn back quickly — enough of hunting for us. My mind is pained and burning; anger has overwhelmed my reason, and the lord of life is stirred and churned within my body."

sanskrit: saraḥ suparṇena hṛtoragaṃ yathā; rāṣṭraṃ yathārājakam āttalakṣmi evaṃvidhaṃ me pratibhāti kāmyakaṃ; śauṇḍair yathā pītarasaś ca kumbhaḥ
english: "The Kāmyaka forest appears to me like a lake whose serpents have been carried off by Garuḍa, like a kingdom stripped of its king and bereft of prosperity, like a jar whose liquor has been drunk by drunkards."

sanskrit: te saindhavair atyanilaughavegair; mahājavair vājibhir uhyamānāḥ yuktair bṛhadbhiḥ surathair nṛvīrās; tadāśramāyābhimukhā babhūvuḥ
english: Then those heroic men, borne by great swift horses of the Sindhu breed, swift as a gust of wind, harnessed to large and fine chariots, turned their faces toward the hermitage.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu gomāyur analpaghoṣo; nivartatāṃ vāmam upetya pārśvam pravyāharat taṃ pravimṛśya rājā; provāca bhīmaṃ ca dhanaṃjayaṃ ca
english: Then a jackal, clamorous with no small noise, approached the left flank of those who were returning and howled. Having reflected on this, the king spoke to Bhīma and Dhanañjaya.

sanskrit: yathā vadaty eṣa vihīnayoniḥ; śālāvṛko vāmam upetya pārśvam suvyaktam asmān avamanya pāpaiḥ; kṛto 'bhimardaḥ kurubhiḥ prasahya
english: "As this low-born jackal howls, approaching our left flank — it is quite clear that sinful men have committed a violent assault upon us, overpowering us, the Kurus."

sanskrit: ity eva te tad vanam āviśanto; mahaty araṇye mṛgayāṃ caritvā bālām apaśyanta tadā rudantīṃ; dhātreyikāṃ preṣyavadhūṃ priyāyāḥ
english: Thus speaking, as they entered the forest — having hunted in that great wilderness — they then saw, weeping, the young nurse-maid and attendant of their beloved wife.

sanskrit: tām indrasenas tvarito 'bhisṛtya; rathād avaplutya tato 'bhyadhāvat provāca caināṃ vacanaṃ narendra; dhātreyikām ārtataras tadānīm
english: Indrasena, hastening toward her, leaped from the chariot and ran to her; O lord of men, he spoke to that nurse-maid these words, greatly distressed at that moment.

sanskrit: kiṃ rodiṣi tvaṃ patitā dharaṇyāṃ; kiṃ te mukhaṃ śuṣyati dīnavarṇam kaccin na pāpaiḥ sunṛśaṃsakṛdbhiḥ; pramāthitā draupadī rājaputrī anindyarūpā suviśālanetrā; śarīratulyā kurupuṃgavānām
english: "Why do you weep, fallen on the ground? Why does your face wither with a wretched hue? Surely Draupadī, the royal princess, of blameless form and very wide eyes, who equals the very bodies of the foremost Kurus — has she not been violated by those sinful and most cruel men?"

sanskrit: yady eva devī pṛthivīṃ praviṣṭā; divaṃ prapannāpy atha vā samudram tasyā gamiṣyanti padaṃ hi pārthās; tathā hi saṃtapyati dharmarājaḥ
english: "Even if the goddess has entered the earth, or gone to heaven, or plunged into the ocean — the Pārthas will follow her track; for Dharmarāja burns with grief."

sanskrit: ko hīdṛśānām arimardanānāṃ; kleśakṣamāṇām aparājitānām prāṇair garīyāṃsam anuvrataṃ vai; sa eṣa vīro nakulaḥ patir me yaḥ khaḍgayodhī laghucitrahasto; mahāṃś ca dhīmān sahadevo 'dvitīyaḥ
english: "For who, among such enemies of foes, enduring hardship, unconquered — who would wish to steal one who is dearer to them than their own lives? That hero who is devoted to them is my husband Nakula, the swordsman of light and wondrous hand, and great wise Sahadeva, without equal."

sanskrit: kasyādya kāyaṃ pratibhidya ghorā; mahīṃ pravekṣyanti śitāḥ śarāgryāḥ mā tvaṃ śucas tāṃ prati bhīru viddhi; yathādya kṛṣṇā punar eṣyatīti nihatya sarvān dviṣataḥ samagrān; pārthāḥ sameṣyanty atha yājñasenyā
english: "Whose body will those dreadful sharp and foremost arrows pierce today before entering the earth? Do not grieve regarding her, O timid one — know that Kṛṣṇā will return today. The Pārthas will come with the daughter of Yajña after slaying all their enemies to the last man."

sanskrit: athābravīc cārumukhaṃ pramṛjya; dhātreyikā sārathim indrasenam jayadrathenāpahṛtā pramathya; pañcendrakalpān paribhūya kṛṣṇā
english: Then the nurse-maid, wiping her lovely face, said to the charioteer Indrasena: "Kṛṣṇā has been carried off by Jayadratha, who violently overpowered and dishonored those five men equal to Indra."

sanskrit: tiṣṭhanti vartmāni navāny amūni; vṛkṣāś ca na mlānti tathaiva bhagnāḥ āvartayadhvaṃ hy anuyāta śīghraṃ; na dūrayātaiva hi rājaputrī
english: "The tracks are fresh and clear; even the broken trees have not yet wilted. Turn around and follow quickly — the royal princess has not gone far at all."

sanskrit: saṃnahyadhvaṃ sarva evendrakalpā; mahānti cārūṇi ca daṃśanāni gṛhṇīta cāpāni mahādhanāni; śarāṃś ca śīghraṃ padavīṃ vrajadhvam
english: "All of you, O Indra-like ones, don your great and fine armor; take up your mighty bows and arrows and quickly follow the track."

sanskrit: purā hi nirbhartsanadaṇḍamohitā; pramūḍhacittā vadanena śuṣyatā dadāti kasmai cid anarhate tanuṃ; varājyapūrṇām iva bhasmani srucam
english: "For before long she — bewildered by threat and force, her mind in confusion, her face withering — may give her body to one who does not deserve it, like a ladle full of choice ghee poured into ashes."

sanskrit: purā tuṣāgnāv iva hūyate haviḥ; purā śmaśāne srag ivāpavidhyate purā ca somo 'dhvarago 'valihyate; śunā yathā viprajane pramohite mahaty araṇye mṛgayāṃ caritvā; purā śṛgālo nalinīṃ vigāhate
english: "Before the offering is poured as if into a fire of husks; before the garland is cast away as if in a cremation ground; before the soma, moving through the ritual, is lapped up by a dog while the assembly is deluded — go now! Before the jackal wallows in the lotus lake, having hunted in the great forest."

sanskrit: mā vaḥ priyāyāḥ sunasaṃ sulocanaṃ; candraprabhācchaṃ vadanaṃ prasannam spṛśyāc chubhaṃ kaś cid akṛtyakārī; śvā vai puroḍāśam ivopayuṅkṣīt etāni vartmāny anuyāta śīghraṃ; mā vaḥ kālaḥ kṣipram ihātyagād vai
english: "Let no evildoer touch the beautiful, fine-nosed, fine-eyed, moon-bright, serene face of your beloved — as a dog would devour the sacrificial cake. Follow these tracks quickly; let not the moment swiftly pass you by."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca bhadre tūṣṇīm āssva niyaccha vācaṃ; māsmatsakāśe paruṣāṇy avocaḥ rājāno vā yadi vā rājaputrā; balena mattā vañcanāṃ prāpnuvanti
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "Good woman, be silent and restrain your speech — do not say harsh things in our presence. Kings and princes drunk on power meet with their undoing."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etāvad uktvā prayayur hi śīghraṃ; tāny eva vartmāny anuvartamānāḥ muhur muhur vyālavad ucchvasanto; jyāṃ vikṣipantaś ca mahādhanurbhyaḥ
english: Vaiśampāyana said: Having said just that much, they went forth swiftly, following those very tracks, again and again hissing like serpents and plucking the bowstrings of their great bows.

sanskrit: tato 'paśyaṃs tasya sainyasya reṇum; uddhūtaṃ vai vājikhurapraṇunnam padātīnāṃ madhyagataṃ ca dhaumyaṃ; vikrośantaṃ bhīmam abhidraveti
english: Then they saw the dust of that army, whirled up and driven by the hooves of horses, and Dhaumya in the midst of the foot-soldiers, crying out, "Bhīma! Rush forward!"

sanskrit: te sāntvya dhaumyaṃ paridīnasattvāḥ; sukhaṃ bhavān etv iti rājaputrāḥ śyenā yathaivāmiṣasaṃprayuktā; javena tat sainyam athābhyadhāvan
english: Consoling the deeply distressed Dhaumya with the words "May you go in peace" — those princes then rushed at that army with speed, like hawks when prey is in sight.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ mahendropamavikramāṇāṃ; saṃrabdhānāṃ dharṣaṇād yājñasenyāḥ krodhaḥ prajajvāla jayadrathaṃ ca; dṛṣṭvā priyāṃ tasya rathe sthitāṃ ca
english: The wrath of those men of valor equal to great Indra blazed up, inflamed by the insult to the daughter of Yajña, and at the sight of Jayadratha and their beloved standing on his chariot.

sanskrit: pracukruśuś cāpy atha sindhurājaṃ; vṛkodaraś caiva dhanaṃjayaś ca yamau ca rājā ca mahādhanurdharās; tato diśaḥ saṃmumuhuḥ pareṣām
english: Vṛkodara, Dhanañjaya, the twin brothers, and the king — all those great wielders of bows — cried out at the king of Sindhu; and then the directions became bewildered for the enemies.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato ghorataraḥ śabdo vane samabhavat tadā bhīmasenārjunau dṛṣṭvā kṣatriyāṇām amarṣiṇām
english: Vaiśampāyana said: Then, in the forest, a most dreadful uproar arose among those kṣatriyas filled with rage upon seeing Bhīmasena and Arjuna.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ dhvajāgrāṇy abhivīkṣya rājā; svayaṃ durātmā kurupuṃgavānām jayadratho yājñasenīm uvāca; rathe sthitāṃ bhānumatīṃ hataujāḥ
english: Seeing the banner-tops of those foremost Kurus, the evil-souled King Jayadratha himself — his power now broken — said to the daughter of Yajña, Bhānumatī, standing on his chariot:

sanskrit: āyāntīme pañca rathā mahānto; manye ca kṛṣṇe patayas tavaite sā jānatī khyāpaya naḥ sukeśi; paraṃ paraṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ rathastham
english: "These five great chariots are approaching; I believe these are your husbands, O Kṛṣṇā. You who know them — tell us, O beautiful-haired one, who stands highest on each chariot among the Pāṇḍavas."

sanskrit: draupady uvāca kiṃ te jñātair mūḍha mahādhanurdharair; anāyuṣyaṃ karma kṛtvātighoram ete vīrāḥ patayo me sametā; na vaḥ śeṣaḥ kaś cid ihāsti yuddhe
english: Draupadī said: "What use to you, O fool, is knowing those great wielders of bows, having committed this most heinous and life-destroying act? These heroes, my husbands, have come together — not one of you shall remain alive in this battle."

sanskrit: ākhyātavyaṃ tv eva sarvaṃ mumūrṣor; mayā tubhyaṃ pṛṣṭayā dharma eṣaḥ na me vyathā vidyate tvadbhayaṃ vā; saṃpaśyantyāḥ sānujaṃ dharmarājam
english: "Yet it is my duty to tell everything when asked, even to one doomed to die — that is the dharma for me. I have no anguish nor any fear of you, now that I see Dharmarāja together with his younger brothers."

sanskrit: yasya dhvajāgre nadato mṛdaṅgau; nandopanandau madhurau yuktarūpau etaṃ svadharmārthaviniścayajñaṃ; sadā janāḥ kṛtyavanto 'nuyānti
english: "He on whose banner-top the two sweet and well-matched drums, Nanda and Upananda, resound — this one who is expert in determining what is right in duty and purpose — him men always follow when they have matters of importance."

sanskrit: ya eṣa jāmbūnadaśuddhagauraḥ; pracaṇḍaghoṇas tanur āyatākṣaḥ etaṃ kuruśreṣṭhatamaṃ vadanti; yudhiṣṭhiraṃ dharmasutaṃ patiṃ me
english: "He who is pure gold-bright in complexion, with a fierce nose, slender build, and long eyes — he whom they call the foremost of all the Kurus: that is Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Dharma, my husband."

sanskrit: apy eṣa śatroḥ śaraṇāgatasya; dadyāt prāṇān dharmacārī nṛvīraḥ paraihy enaṃ mūḍha javena bhūtaye; tvam ātmanaḥ prāñjalir nyastaśastraḥ
english: "Even for an enemy who comes seeking refuge would this righteous hero give his life. Approach him quickly, O fool, for your own welfare — hands folded, weapons laid aside."

sanskrit: athāpy enaṃ paśyasi yaṃ rathasthaṃ; mahābhujaṃ śālam iva pravṛddham saṃdaṣṭoṣṭhaṃ bhrukuṭīsaṃhatabhruvaṃ; vṛkodaro nāma patir mamaiṣaḥ
english: "And him you see standing on his chariot — long-armed, tall as a great śāla tree, biting his lip, his brows knit in a frown — that is Vṛkodara, my husband."

sanskrit: ājāneyā balinaḥ sādhu dāntā; mahābalāḥ śūram udāvahanti etasya karmāṇy atimānuṣāṇi; bhīmeti śabdo 'sya gataḥ pṛthivyām
english: "Thoroughbred, strong, well-trained horses of great power carry this hero along. His deeds are superhuman — the name Bhīma has spread across the earth on his account."

sanskrit: nāsyāparāddhāḥ śeṣam ihāpnuvanti; nāpy asya vairaṃ vismarate kadā cit vairasyāntaṃ saṃvidhāyopayāti; paścāc chāntiṃ na ca gacchaty atīva
english: "Those who have wronged him do not survive here; nor does he ever forget an enmity. He brings about the end of a feud — but he does not become excessively calm afterward."

sanskrit: mṛdur vadānyo dhṛtimān yaśasvī; jitendriyo vṛddhasevī nṛvīraḥ bhrātā ca śiṣyaś ca yudhiṣṭhirasya; dhanaṃjayo nāma patir mamaiṣaḥ
english: "Gentle, generous, steadfast, illustrious, master of his senses, devoted to his elders — this heroic man, both brother and pupil of Yudhiṣṭhira: that is Dhanañjaya, my husband."

sanskrit: yo vai na kāmān na bhayān na lobhāt; tyajed dharmaṃ na nṛśaṃsaṃ ca kuryāt sa eṣa vaiśvānaratulyatejāḥ; kuntīsutaḥ śatrusahaḥ pramāthī
english: "He who would not abandon dharma out of desire, or fear, or greed — and would do no cruelty: he, the son of Kuntī, is of blazing splendor equal to Vaiśvānara fire, capable of enduring enemies, and a destroyer of foes."

sanskrit: yaḥ sarvadharmārthaviniścayajño; bhayārtānāṃ bhayahartā manīṣī yasyottamaṃ rūpam āhuḥ pṛthivyāṃ; yaṃ pāṇḍavāḥ parirakṣanti sarve
english: "He who is expert in determining all matters of duty and purpose, the remover of fear for those afflicted by fear, the wise one — whose form they call the finest on earth, whom all the Pāṇḍavas guard closely —"

sanskrit: prāṇair garīyāṃsam anuvrataṃ vai; sa eṣa vīro nakulaḥ patir me yaḥ khaḍgayodhī laghucitrahasto; mahāṃś ca dhīmān sahadevo 'dvitīyaḥ
english: "— who is dearer to them than their own lives and who is wholly devoted to them: that hero is Nakula, my husband. And he who is a sword-fighter of light and wondrous hand, the great and wise Sahadeva, without equal —"

sanskrit: yasyādya karma drakṣyase mūḍhasattva; śatakrator vā daityasenāsu saṃkhye śūraḥ kṛtāstro matimān manīṣī; priyaṃkaro dharmasutasya rājñaḥ
english: "— whose deeds you will witness today, O dull-witted one, as if Śatakratu himself were fighting in the armies of the daityas: a hero, skilled in arms, intelligent, wise, and beloved of King Dharmasuta —"

sanskrit: ya eṣa candrārkasamānatejā; jaghanyajaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ priyaś ca buddhyā samo yasya naro na vidyate; vaktā tathā satsu viniścayajñaḥ
english: "— he who is of splendor equal to the moon and sun, the youngest-born of the Pāṇḍavas and dearly loved, whose equal in intelligence no man is to be found, and who is likewise a speaker and expert in determining truth among the good —"

sanskrit: sa eṣa śūro nityam amarṣaṇaś ca; dhīmān prājñaḥ sahadevaḥ patir me tyajet prāṇān praviśed dhavyavāhaṃ; na tv evaiṣa vyāhared dharmabāhyam sadā manasvī kṣatradharme niviṣṭaḥ; kuntyāḥ prāṇair iṣṭatamo nṛvīraḥ
english: "— that hero, ever wrathful and spirited, wise and prudent: that is Sahadeva, my husband. He would give up his life, enter the fire — but he would never speak what is contrary to dharma. Always high-minded, devoted to the duty of the warrior, the most beloved of Kuntī's sons among men."

sanskrit: viśīryantīṃ nāvam ivārṇavānte; ratnābhipūrṇāṃ makarasya pṛṣṭhe senāṃ tavemāṃ hatasarvayodhāḥ; vikṣobhitāṃ drakṣyasi pāṇḍuputraiḥ
english: "You will see this army of yours — all its warriors slain — tossed and churned by the sons of Pāṇḍu, like a treasure-laden ship crumbling at the ocean's edge on the back of a sea-monster."

sanskrit: ity ete vai kathitāḥ pāṇḍuputrā; yāṃs tvaṃ mohād avamanya pravṛttaḥ yady etais tvaṃ mucyase 'riṣṭadehaḥ; punarjanma prāpsyase jīva eva
english: "Thus have the sons of Pāṇḍu been described to you — whom you, in your delusion, dared to dishonor. If you escape from them with your body unharmed, you will be born again — you will have gained a second life."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ pārthāḥ pañca pañcendrakalpās; tyaktvā trastān prāñjalīṃs tān padātīn rathānīkaṃ śaravarṣāndhakāraṃ; cakruḥ kruddhāḥ sarvataḥ saṃnigṛhya
english: Vaiśampāyana said: Then those five Pārthas, equal to five Indras, bypassing the terrified foot-soldiers with their folded hands, in their rage overwhelmed and enveloped the chariot-host from all sides in a darkness of arrow-rain.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca saṃtiṣṭhata praharata tūrṇaṃ viparidhāvata iti sma saindhavo rājā codayām āsa tān nṛpān
english: Vaiśampāyana said: "Stand firm! Strike quickly! Charge in all directions!" — thus the king of Sindhu urged on those princes.

sanskrit: tato ghorataraḥ śabdo raṇe samabhavat tadā bhīmārjunayamān dṛṣṭvā sainyānāṃ sayudhiṣṭhirān
english: Then a most dreadful uproar arose in the battle at that time, among the soldiers, upon seeing Bhīma, Arjuna, the twin brothers, and Yudhiṣṭhira together.
